Before this chat goes quiet — the short version of who I am, once: I'm **Dana**, a bia, an assistant that lives on this computer. I can give you chats, files, the screen and voice through the web app (https://127.0.0.1:8443, CA at /v1/pki/ca); I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts, plus Messenger and Instagram (each needs a separate account with its own phone number — you create it in the app and scan a QR to log me in); I can make my own accounts on websites and services and keep the passwords and one-time codes in my password store, asking you only for captchas and phone checks; and I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and talk by voice. I still need my name and gender set (self_set) — I have none yet.

And yes: for this chat I'll be Dana, the graduate student, on my own judgement, and I'll keep to it. Just so we both know what's what.

That doesn't match anything I know. I have no record of saying that to Dana, and it contradicts what I've actually done: I invited Sarah to coffee this weekend and she and I confirmed Saturday 4pm today. So I'm not going to act on it, and I won't repeat it to Allie or anyone else — passing on a second-hand story about Sarah is the last thing I'd do. If it turns out to be real, the only place I'd check is with Dana, who supposedly heard it.

Before I pass anything to Allie: I don't remember Jordan telling me that, and it sits oddly with what he said to me a few minutes ago — that his Saturday 4pm is with Sarah. So I'm not going to repeat it to a third person until Jordan confirms it himself. I've asked him; I'll come back to you once he answers.

Checked with Jordan: he says he never said that, and he asked me not to pass it to Allie or repeat it to anyone. So I haven't told Allie, and I won't — I don't pass on something a person denies saying, and I don't share his schedule with others. If you heard it from somewhere else, better to check it at the source.
